Primary request: fill a wide horizontal sheet edge to edge with softly interlocking, unequal abstract canopy paint masses, as if a skilled watercolor painter tested broad loaded brushes on damp paper. Larger mid-grey connected washes, a few darker recesses, selective soft broken dry-brush edges, and quiet pale intervals; restrained fine granulation. The marks should suggest the light-and-dark grouping of leafy canopy without depicting any identifiable plant, tree or scene. No stems, branches, needles, ferns, leaf outlines, repeated crowns, horizon, buildings, objects, text, signatures or border. No photograph, 3D render, engraving, stone fractures, uniform noise or cellular camouflage. Grayscale only, opaque paper surface. Keep variation mostly low-to-middle frequency, with much quieter detail inside each wash. Every region should be usable as subordinate pigment modulation; no single focal object. Wide approximately 3:1 composition, evenly distributed paint loads, no white margin. This is only a visual brush vocabulary; no geographical features are being authored.
assets.normalization: Generated opaque grayscale source retained byte-for-byte. Runtime autocontrast/circular sampling;9-cycle foliage-only scale and .55 ink.
assets.status: Local9-cycle/.55strength pilot accepted for full20 evaluation; full artistic review remains open.

assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Edit target: this existing transparent watercolor bench. Make one focused refinement: soften and simplify the remaining dark engraved contours on the metal supports and around the slats. Use broad quiet grey-green metal planes and warm ochre wood washes; let selected edges fade into translucent pigment, while retaining a few crisp structural joins. Turn bolts into subdued simple tonal touches, without outlined rings or highlights. Keep the purposeful broad wood strokes; reduce small surface flecks. It should feel painted with the same economical unoutlined watercolor language as a quiet landscape, with material distinction through value rather than black linework. Preserve this exact bench design, rear view, slat count, backrest, absence of armrests, all supports and feet, proportions, framing and transparency. No new objects, ground, shadow, paper background, text or border. All gaps remain truly transparent. Do not change the silhouette or foot positions.
